title: Need to fix critical services verification in platform test cases
author: yvolynets-mlnx
body:

**Description**

Need to fix functionality in platform test cases which verifies critical services are running.
It seems that swss service doesn’t use “docker wait swss” in the latest master any longer. Instead, it uses “/usr/bin/docker-wait-any ${SERVICE} ${PEER}”. This is done in commit https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/commit/85b0de3df1125ad291afe0c7c93628dd45f226db.

<!--
Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Run platform test cases:
```py.test --inventory ../ansible/inventory --host-pattern [HOST] --module-path ../ansible/library/ --testbed [HOST]-[TOPO] --testbed_file ../ansible/testbed.csv --show-capture=no --log-cli-level info -ra -v platform/test_reboot.py```

**Describe the results you received:**
```
01:00:52     def check_critical_services(dut):
01:00:52         """
01:00:52         @summary: Use systemctl to check whether all the critical services have expected status. ActiveState of all
01:00:52             services must be "active". SubState of all services must be "running".
01:00:52         @param dut: The AnsibleHost object of DUT. For interacting with DUT.
01:00:52         """
01:00:52         logging.info("Wait until all critical services are fully started")
01:00:52 >       assert wait_until(300, 20, dut.critical_services_fully_started), "Not all critical services are fully started"
01:00:52 E       AssertionError: Not all critical services are fully started
```


**Describe the results you expected:**
Method which verifies that all critical services are running should be updated to ensure that all services are verifying correctly. Pay attention to the swss service.

**Additional information you deem important:**
```
SONiC Software Version: SONiC.HEAD.123-c07ae3b1
```

### Description of PR
<!--

-->

### Summary

Instead of checking for the whether a `docker wait <service_name>` command is running to determine whether a service is fully started, instead we check whether or not the container itself is running using `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' <service_name>`.

Fixes https://github.com/Azure/sonic-mgmt/issues/1215

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] Test case(new/improvement)

### Approach
#### How did you do it?

Instead of checking for the whether a `docker wait <service_name>` command is running to determine whether a service is fully started, instead we check whether or not the container itself is running using `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' <service_name>`.
